haiku-low.q1: reports.row_count decides: 10,000 or fewer streams CSV directly in the HTTP response; more than 10,000 returns 202 and a background job emails a 24-hour link.
haiku-low.q2: The second request is rejected by the unique index and the existing queued or running export is returned; nothing new is enqueued, and it may use different filters, which the page shows.
haiku-low.q3: The emailed link works for 24 hours. The bucket's lifecycle rule deletes the file 7 days after creation; there is no cleanup job. The download endpoint returns 410 after 7 days.
haiku-low.q4: Up to 3 attempts (MAX_ATTEMPTS). After the final failure, the row is set to failed and the user gets a report_export_failed email linking to the report page; the page shows failed.
haiku-low.q5: The read replica. The primary holds only the new report_exports table, which is not report data.
haiku-low.q6: In the report_exports row on the primary. The page polls GET /exports/latest every 5 seconds while queued or running, and reads the current state on page load.
haiku-low.q7: It streams: pages 5,000 rows from the replica by row_id, buffers to 8 MB, and uploads parts via multipart. Only one page and one buffer are held, never the whole report.
haiku-low.q8: Parts stay invisible until complete_multipart, so nothing partial is readable. On exception the upload is aborted and the error re-raised; the next attempt starts a new upload from the beginning of the report.
haiku-low.q9: Normalised filters and cols are saved in the report_exports row at click time. The job receives only export_id and loads the view from that row.
haiku-low.q10: A partial unique index on (user_id, report_id) WHERE state IN ('queued','running') in the primary database; the second insert is rejected.
haiku-low.q11: complete_multipart must have made the object visible and the row must be done. A rerun with done and no ready_email_sent_at only resends the email; if already sent it returns. It never rebuilds the file.
haiku-low.q12: NOT STATED for a partial-failure policy beyond this: if the replica errors mid-stream, the connection is aborted so the browser sees a failed download. There is no retry; the user clicks again.

sonnet.q1: Server reads reports.row_count (unfiltered total). 10,000 or fewer: small path, the HTTP response is the CSV itself (attachment, streamed), nothing stored. More than 10,000: large path, immediate 202 response with the export record, a background job builds the file and emails the user a link valid 24 hours.
sonnet.q2: The unique partial index on (user_id, report_id) WHERE state IN ('queued','running') rejects the insert; the server returns the existing export and enqueues nothing. It may have different filters, and the page shows which. (Rows queued/running with updated_at older than 2 hours are treated as orphaned, marked failed, and a fresh insert proceeds.)
sonnet.q3: The emailed link (signed_url) works 24 hours. The bucket's existing lifecycle rule deletes every object 7 days after creation; no cleanup job is built.
sonnet.q4: At most 3 attempts (MAX_ATTEMPTS), with 60 s wait before attempt 2 and 300 s before attempt 3. After the final failure, on_final_failure sets state=failed with a short error and sends a report_export_failed email (with link to the report page). The page shows 'failed' with the reason and lets the user start a new export.
sonnet.q5: The read replica, for all report rows (both small and large paths). The primary holds only the report_exports table; the status endpoint reads that from the primary.
sonnet.q6: In the report_exports row on the primary (state queued/running/done/failed). The page polls GET /api/reports/{id}/exports/latest every 5 seconds while queued or running, stopping on done or failed. A returning user calls the same endpoint on page load and sees the current state. A failed poll keeps the last known state and retries next tick.
sonnet.q7: It streams: a multipart upload to the exports bucket. It pages the replica by keyset (row_id, LIMIT 5000), appends CSV text to a buffer, uploads a part whenever the buffer reaches 8 MB, then uploads the remainder as the last part. Only one page (~2 MB) and one buffer (8 MB) are held at a time, about 10 to 30 MB total; the whole report is never in memory. About 400 queries and 113 parts for 900 MB.
sonnet.q8: Nothing is visible, since no object exists until complete_multipart. On an exception the job aborts the multipart upload and re-raises for retry. If the worker is killed or times out, the next attempt aborts the saved upload_id (step 7); anything left is dropped by the bucket's 24-hour incomplete-multipart rule. The next attempt restarts from the beginning (no progress kept), with a new multipart upload and the same payload.
sonnet.q9: They are sent in the POST request, normalised, and saved in the filters and cols columns of the report_exports row (primary). The job payload is only {export_id}; the job loads the row to get the view.
sonnet.q10: The database's unique partial index on (user_id, report_id) WHERE state IN ('queued','running'). Only one insert can succeed; the other is rejected and gets the existing export.
sonnet.q11: complete_multipart must have succeeded (file visible), the row updated to state=done with object_key, finished_at, and a signed URL created, all before the email is sent. If run again when state=done: the job does not rebuild the file; if ready_email_sent_at is empty it creates the link, sends the email and records it; otherwise it just returns. (A crash between sending and recording can send the email twice.)
sonnet.q12: If the replica errors mid-stream (or the 60-second request kill hits), the connection is aborted so the browser sees a failed download, not a clean end that would look like a complete truncated file. There is no retry; the user clicks again.
